catch_records.source_excerpt: The Sea Watch on their full-day trip returned with 280 Yellowfin Tuna, 3 Dorado, 13 Skipjack Tuna and 3 Yellowtail for 28 anglers. Passports are not currently required for these trips. Current sniper-style jigs have been getting bit well, but it’s also a good idea to bring a 20–30 lb live-bait setup.

southern_california.text: The marine pattern is fairly steady through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 4-13 kt; morning is favored on 7 of 7 days. Combined seas range 2.0-5.0 ft with 6-12 sec periods. Best current windows: 09-27 AM, 09-30 AM, 10-02 AM. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The fishing was good for the anglers who went up the coast. There were some nice halibut, rock fish, and sea bass caught near 4 Mile. The Capitola area was a little slower for anglers but they did get a few halibut. The wind was down in the morning but it did blow in the afternoon. The swell is still small.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast September 24, 2026 Big Kings Staging at Chetco River Mouth Customers fishing with Capt. Rye Phillips of Brookings Fishing Charters hold salmon caught in the Chetco estuary over the weekend. Photo courtesy of Brookings Fishing Charters If you’ve been missing the thrill of hooking and landing ocean-fresh, large king salmon, you’ll want to keep your eyes on the Chetco River estuary. Salmon have been staging in tidewater since early September, waiting for enough rain to push upriver. According to Andy Martin of Wild Rivers Fishing, fishing at the mouth of the Chetco is already approaching peak-season catch rates — an encouraging sign for what could be a strong fall run. “Big numbers of kings are staging near the mouth, moving in and out with the tides,” Martin said. “Aside from steady action in the estuary, bottom-fishing anglers are encountering salmon frequently out of Brookings.” Trolling anchovies or herring, with or without 360 flashers, has been producing the best results. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: The Surfrider had a really good trip this morning after the bottom fish and Lingcod and came home with limits on the rockfish and a dozen or so nice Lingcod. They also captured 134 crabs for the folks onboard. Tomorrow looks extremely likely that all the boats in the harbor will be tied to the boards as we have a Gale warning in effect for the area from 11pm this evening thru Friday afternoon. At this time of year normally happens Saturday morning looks great with very little wind and nice seas. See ya then.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: The guys went back to the same spot and after hunting around for awhile they had 30 plus fish stop to end the day with over 40 fish. Some were monsters and most were regular sized tuna. We are sitting out the big wind event tomorrow and headed out again Saturday. ​Mike C 9/23. Lots of smaller fish, but not many monsters.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
